culturalBackground: Full-hand mehndi covers the hand from the fingertips to the wrist and often continues up the forearm.
It is the usual choice for brides and for major festivals where a heavier look is wanted.
A detailed full-hand design can take an hour or more per hand.
Full-hand layouts usually combine several motifs, such as a mandala, a jaal (net) and paisleys, in separate sections.
applicationTips: Plan the layout in sections before you begin so the design stays balanced from fingers to wrist.
Take short breaks between sections; a steady hand matters more than speed.
Have someone help with food and drink, because both hands will be out of use until the paste dries.

faqPool.q: How long does full-hand mehndi take?
faqPool.a: It depends on the detail. A moderate design takes around an hour per hand, and dense bridal work takes longer.

faqPool.q: Is full-hand mehndi only for brides?
faqPool.a: No. It is also popular for Eid, Karva Chauth, Teej and family weddings.

faqPool.q: Should both hands have the same full-hand design?
faqPool.a: They can match, mirror each other, or use two related designs. Mirrored designs are the most traditional.
